title: Following your "Pearls of the Costa Brava: Tossa de Mar" — the sea route from Blanes
content:
Hi Andy,

I enjoyed your "Pearls of the Costa Brava: Tossa de Mar" piece. I'm Iván, from Costa Brava Rent a Boat: we rent boats from Blanes harbour with our own fleet.

For grown-up travellers who want to reach Tossa the scenic way, the natural route is by sea from Blanes, past Lloret and a string of quiet coves. We wrote an honest guide with real distances, which boat suits a half day versus a full day, and the rules for boating without a licence (up to 2 nautical miles, RD 875/2014).

The guide:
https://www.costabravarentaboat.com/es/blog/alquiler-barco-tossa-de-mar-desde-blanes?utm_source=outreach&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=outreach-2026-07-30-calas-fondeo&utm_content=grown-up-travel-guide

title: A boating resource for your "Blanes, Lloret de Mar & Tossa de Mar" guide
content:
Hi NjOY! team,

Your "Blanes, Lloret de Mar & Tossa de Mar" guide is one of the best local overviews of the southern Costa Brava. I'm Iván, from Costa Brava Rent a Boat, renting boats from Blanes harbour with our own fleet.

One angle readers often miss: the three towns connect beautifully by sea, and the coves in between (Cala Bona, Sa Forcanera, Cala Pola) are best reached by boat. We've documented the routes honestly, including how boating without a licence works here.
